column10: Do not equate the thick-print graphic with a conclusively first-built unit; enclosure, pot dates, knobs and other features overlap.

column10: Enclosure brow geometry is a useful external dating clue; avoid treating pot date codes alone as exact assembly dates.

column10: Short-board conversion is a specimen-level state and should not be treated as a separate family.

column6: Sola Sound-built Vox-branded MKII production followed the Sola Sound-branded version, with early examples sometimes showing graphics modified over Sola Sound branding.
column9: Preserve Vox as retail brand and Sola Sound as documented builder/OEM relationship.

column6: Marshall Supa Fuzz examples from this period are Sola Sound-built Tone Bender MKII family products with Marshall branding.
column9: Treat Supa Fuzz as an OEM-branded member of the Tone Bender family, not an unrelated distortion design.

column6: Rotosound was among the companies supplied by Sola Sound with the MKII-family fuzz design during the 1966-1968 period.
column9: Brand/OEM relationship is more historically useful than assigning a standalone circuit genealogy.

column9: Early-country-of-production details remain subject to reconciliation; do not overstate a precise first Italian batch date.

column6: Teisco TF-1 is documented as a Japanese FY-6 Super Fuzz family product and should remain distinct from the separate Teisco Fuzz Machine lineage.
column9: Use exact model naming and FY-6-family relationship as the primary identification clues.

column9: External enclosure and branding changes should be reconciled before assigning tight sub-periods.

column9: Keep the March 1968 ad appearance as stronger evidence than older generic 1969-71 estimates.

column9: OEM attribution to Honey-labeled layouts remains a research proposition rather than a definitive manufacturing claim.

column9: Useful non-Macari/Sola benchmark for the diversity of late-1960s British fuzz.

column6: Early Park Fuzz Sound examples from 1969 are Sola Sound-branded/OEM fuzz products using the Tone Bender MKIII family.
column9: Preserve Park branding while linking the documented Sola Sound OEM relationship.

column9: Enclosure family is the key external distinction; do not infer exact transition dates without specimen evidence.

column9: Preserve early Bud Box and later big-box production as specimen/format states within one family.

column9: Keep early production revisions separate from later BOSS overdrive models.

column10: Do not make the silicon transition an exact single-date boundary; evidence indicates overlap.
